name: Scratched Metal 55
notes: A worked metal surface: one merged scratch history, 55% near-linear and 45% deep-swirl strokes with heavy-tailed lengths, widths and depths, gating a solid primary. TONAL dual-gate: the mask is the tone-mapped texture field itself, not a threshold cut, so the stroke carries the texture as graded alpha and a window from a stroke matches the designed height field. The level number is the damage/modulation DEPTH (contrast dial): damage is a delta from the intact material, so moderate damage = moderate contrast - per review. Two deconvolutions bind the stroke to the design (docs/fractal-texture-math.md): the spectral 1/H pre-compensation on the field's fbm band, and the value-curve inverse v = 1-(depth*damage)^(1/n) that undoes the mask train's ~n-stamp over-compositing. Threshold-cut coverage masks were the first shipped form and were revised on review (maximal contrast everywhere, stroke windows unlike the swatch fields). Mapping delta+invert: the intact metal renders as a mid-tone wash and the scratch history carves DARKER marks into it. Worked: legible scratch web over toned metal. Tips from tips/scratched-metal.spec.json; audited by tools/spectrum-audit.mjs. REVISED after splotch review (dark/light discs at stroke width): dual scatter 0.7->0.2 makes the per-point stamp count deterministic (composite tone = v^n), and the tip field carries no content coarser than the stamp, so no stamp tints its whole footprint. Dual spacing 0.14 (not the family 0.28): the flat metal background exposes the rigid-train comb that busier textures bury, and deeper overlap both halves the beads period and doubles the averaging.
